intended_object: For a subgroup G of the symmetric group Sym(α), with α finite, and a multiset μ (a partition of |α|), this is the finite set of conjugacy classes of G whose elements have full cycle type μ, where fixed points count as 1-cycles. The object is taken from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body keeps exactly the classes C in `ConjClasses G` that have some representative g in G whose full cycle type is mu. The full cycle type is defined in the library as `cycleType + replicate (card α - support.card) 1`, which is the same as the parts of Mathlib's `Equiv.Perm.partition`, i.e. the textbook cycle type with fixed points included.

Elements that are conjugate in G are also conjugate in Sym(α), so they have the same cycle type. Hence "some representative has type mu" is the same as "every member has type mu", as the docstring says. The lemma `mem_classesOfFullCycleType_mk` in the same file proves this.

Degenerate cases also behave as intended:
- If mu is not the type of any element of G, the result is the empty set.
- One cycle type can split into several G-classes, and all of them are included.

Generality: a subgroup of Perm α on a finite carrier is the natural setting for permutation groups. A finite carrier is needed for the full cycle type, since it counts fixed points. Mathlib has no definition of this set of classes.
